gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI stations ship with ECO mode turned on, and that ECO cuts the AC outlets after a stretch of low or no load. The BLUETTI manual itself says to turn ECO off for refrigerators. A fridge that cycles off can drop below the threshold and lose power overnight, and that can happen on an otherwise correctly sized weekend setup.
standout_why: I checked the three cited rival pages and our own page. Anker SOLIX's 'Complete Off-Grid Cabin Solar Setup Guide' and 'Off Grid Solar Cabin Essentials Checklist' mention fridge loads and general startup surge, but say nothing about ECO or auto-off, standby draw or charging temperature. SolutionEnergy's 'Off-Grid Cabin Power Systems' says a fridge 'cycles on and off' and that unheated cabins freeze ('Follow the maker's temperature limits'), but it has no auto-off mechanism and no number. Our current Dealectric page covers inverter idle draw (10–20 W) but not ECO auto-off or the 32°F charging limit. None of these pages links the fridge's on/off cycling to the station's default low-load shutoff.
decides: It does not change the size. 2 kWh with 350–400 W of panels, or 3 kWh, still fits the load. It does decide whether the fridge stays powered through the weekend. On the Elite 200 V2 and AC180, which are both on our page, ECO must be turned off before leaving the fridge plugged in. This is a setup step the answer should state. For a November trip there is a second check: the Elite 200 V2 manual lists charging at 0–40°C (32–104°F). If the station is below freezing, solar can't refill it, so the battery has to cover the whole weekend on its own. That points to the larger-battery option (3 kWh or more), or to keeping the station inside the heated part of the cabin.

findings.label: ECO mode default and BLUETTI's own advice for fridges
findings.value: "AC-ECO and DC-ECO modes are enabled by default." "The Elite 200 V2 shuts off the AC or DC output after a period of low or no load." "Disable the ECO mode when connecting small devices under 60W or critical appliances such as lights and refrigerators."
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 User Manual (V1.2), section 5.4 ECO Mode, ManualsLib
findings.note: This is a ManualsLib copy of the maker's V1.2 manual. BLUETTI's own PDFs (s4.bluettipower.com US EN V2.0 and V1.2) were over 10 MB or would not extract as text, and bluettipower.com/products redirect-looped. The manual also says pressing the AC power button turns AC-ECO and DC-ECO on or off together, and the app controls them separately. A small fridge averages roughly 25–50 W, and its compressor-off periods draw close to 0 W, so a long off-cycle in a cool cabin can trip the low-load timer. That last point is my reasoning from BLUETTI's 60 W advice, not a figure BLUETTI gives.

findings.label: AC-ECO while charging from AC
findings.value: "AC-ECO mode is not available when charging with AC power."
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 User Manual (V1.2), section 5.4 ECO Mode, ManualsLib
findings.note: Off-grid, there is no AC charging, so the shutoff can happen. Solar charging is not mentioned as an exception.

findings.label: Charging and discharging temperature
findings.value: Charging 0°C to 40°C (32°F to 104°F); discharging −20°C to 40°C (−4°F to 104°F)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 User Manual (V1.2), specifications (printed p. 22), ManualsLib
findings.note: The station can power the fridge down to −4°F but can't accept solar below 32°F. In a cabin left unheated in November, the panel can't refill the battery until the station warms up. The manual has no self-heating text, only a 'Low Temperature' LCD icon.

findings.label: ECO mode trigger thresholds
findings.value: AC output turns off below a set 10–30 W, and DC output below a set 5–10 W, after 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 manual, section 5.1 FAQs (printed p. 16), ManualsLib.de
findings.note: Quote: "the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while"; "set the power threshold of AC output and DC output to 10-30W /5-10W, respectively" "for 1, 2, 3, or 4 hours." The FAQ is in English on a German-language mirror. This page does not state whether ECO is on by default.
